title: Ink-Scent Private School
premise: A long private-school calligraphy drama. Aqin and Aqing look nearly alike and are easily mistaken; the Duan inkstone goes intact→cracked→repaired; the bamboo book chest burns and must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_teacher: Calligraphy teacher Shen Chuan around fifty, lean face, indigo jacket over a gray cloth long robe, always a soft ink smell on the cuffs, quiet look.
states.weary_wounded: The same Shen Chuan: gauze on the temple, leaning on a bamboo cane, indigo jacket torn at the shoulder, eyes tired.
states.deceased: Shen Chuan has closed his eyes and passed away, lying quietly on a bamboo couch in the study, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.young_apprentice: Young Aqin: a lean calligraphy apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, gray short jacket, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Adult Aqin: a steady young calligrapher in the twenties, still the indigo headscarf, short jacket swapped for a deep-cyan long robe.

states.intact: An old purple-black Duan inkstone with cloud-and-bat patterns on the side, ink pool deep and even, stone body warm and fine.
states.cracked: The same Duan inkstone with a fine crack across the pool; ink seeps into the fissure, uneven color.
states.repaired: After kintsugi repair the Duan inkstone can be used again; fine gold lines fill the crack; the pool holds clear ink once more.

states.intact: A thread-bound copybook with a cloth cover, pages of student faults and stroke demos in neat small kai.
states.ink_stained: The same copybook soaked through by spilled ink, cover wrinkled, notes bled into blotches.

states.intact: A bamboo book chest branded with the character Shen on the lid, holding xuan paper and copy slips, tight mortise joints.
states.burned: The bamboo book chest has collapsed into a charred wreck; only a remnant of the Shen brand remains.

states.young_peer: Young peer Aqing whose face closely resembles Aqin's, but a cream silk scarf and a bamboo-leaf jade hairpin at the temple, flamboyant look.
states.remade_face: After remaking the look, Aqing still wears the cream silk scarf; the bamboo-leaf jade hairpin remains, expression deeper.

E7.name: Ink-Scent study
E7.appearance: Bamboo-blind half-rolled private-school study; a writing desk on blue brick at center; scrolls on the wall; air rich with pine-soot ink.

E8.name: stele-corridor outer court
E8.appearance: The bluestone stele corridor outside the study; old stele rubbings stand on both sides; ivy on the pillars; mottled afternoon light.

E9.name: alley-mouth brush shop
E9.appearance: A brush-and-ink shop at the narrow alley mouth; brush racks and inkstones on a wooden counter; signboard reading Drunken Ink Studio; busy with people.

E10.name: old school porch
E10.appearance: The private school's old porch; gray tiles drip; the lintel plaque Yang Zheng is mottled; moss on the stone steps.

E11.name: memorial wood plaque
E11.appearance: A cypress plaque nailed to the porch pillar, carved with Shen Chuan's name and teaching years, edges worm-eaten.

E12.name: leisure seals
E12.appearance: Three Shoushan-stone leisure seals carved Yang Zheng, Ink Affinity, and Quiet Mind, strung on a red cord at the desk corner.

E13.name: paulownia painting box
E13.appearance: A paulownia painting box with gold cloud patterns on the face, no Shen brand, flatter and wider than the bamboo book chest.

E14.name: county-school prefect
E14.appearance: A lean county-school prefect in gray robe and blue cap, copper badge on the shoulder, build somewhat like Shen Chuan's but more rigid.

E15.name: weasel-hair brushes
E15.appearance: A row of five weasel-hair brushes hung on the study brush rack, red-paper numbers on the shafts, tips neat.

E16.name: bronze paperweights
E16.appearance: Two crouching-lion bronze paperweights pressing both ends of the desk, lion bodies with a quiet patina glow.

E17.name: Xiaotao
E17.appearance: Alley-mouth brush-shop girl Xiaotao in a light-brown headscarf and gray cloth clothes; at a glance like young Aqin, but a sharper chin and shy unfamiliar eyes.

E18.name: imitation Duan inkstone
E18.appearance: A smaller imitation Duan inkstone with no cloud-and-bat side pattern, black pottery base.

E19.name: paper merchant Lao Gu
E19.appearance: Paper merchant Lao Gu delivering xuan, bamboo hat and bamboo basket on the back, full beard, build like Shen Chuan's but sturdier.

segments.action: At dusk, Shen Chuan lifts the bamboo blind and enters the Ink-Scent study, first checking the Duan inkstone on the desk.
A row of five weasel-hair brushes hangs on the study brush rack; Shen Chuan neatens each tip.
Two crouching-lion bronze paperweights press both ends of the desk; Shen Chuan lifts one to feel its weight.
Shen Chuan circles the desk checking whether the xuan is damp and wrinkled.
From the window Shen Chuan watches the bluestone of the stele-corridor outer court darken.
Lamp light mirrors in the Duan inkstone pool; Shen Chuan gently blows away the foam.
Shen Chuan sits on a bamboo chair in the study corner for a brief rest.
Shen Chuan opens the copybook, dips ink, and notes the students' common faults of the day.
Shen Chuan draws a na-stroke demo curve in the copybook.
Shen Chuan closes the copybook and returns it to the wooden box beside the desk.
Residual ink by the Duan inkstone dries; Shen Chuan adds a spoon of clear water.
Shen Chuan blows dry the fresh notes so the page edges will not stick.
In the morning stele-corridor outer court, Shen Chuan greets young Aqin arriving with the bamboo book chest on the back.
Aqin sets down the bamboo book chest and brushes mud flecks from the lid.
Shen Chuan points to the three leisure seals strung on a red cord at the desk corner and teaches Aqin to read the seal texts.
Aqin crouches under the stele corridor, tracing broken strokes on the stele with a finger.
Shen Chuan explains hidden-tip starts; Aqin nods carefully.
Aqin glances back at the bamboo book chest, eyes full of care.
Shen Chuan has Aqin grind half a pool of pale ink, then copy three lines of large characters.
In the noisy alley-mouth brush shop, Aqing in a cream silk scarf looks up from behind the counter.

segments.action: In plum-rain season, Shen Chuan spreads damp xuan sheet by sheet to dry in the Ink-Scent study.
Shen Chuan pads wool felt under the desk so blue brick damp will not bleed the ink.
At dawn, Shen Chuan takes a rubbing of broken characters from an old stele in the stele-corridor outer court.
Shen Chuan clamps the new rubbing between boards, pressed by the two bronze paperweights to air-dry.
At high summer noon, Shen Chuan lowers the bamboo blind, leaving only a slit of light on the Duan inkstone.
Shen Chuan washes overnight ink dregs from the brush washer into the soak pit behind the study.
When autumn wind rises, Shen Chuan stores scrolls in the wall cupboard so they will not be blown down.
On a blank copybook page Shen Chuan tries a few lines of slender-gold script, then tears them and rewrites.
On a Frost's Descent night, Shen Chuan lights an oil lamp and checks stroke starts and finishes against the stele copy.
Shen Chuan wraps the bamboo book chest in a blanket, fearing night dew will harm the paper.
On a heavy-snow day, Shen Chuan sweeps thin snow from the old school porch stone steps.
Shen Chuan warms hands with breath and grinds ink; scent slowly fills the cold study.
In early spring, Shen Chuan trims ivy on the stele corridor, uncovering hidden inscriptions.
Shen Chuan dips each of the five weasel-hair brushes in water to open the tip and checks belly spring.
Shen Chuan hangs a newly written Yang Zheng horizontal scroll in a study corner.
Around the Dragon Boat Festival, Shen Chuan smokes the bookcase with mugwort to drive bookworms.
Shen Chuan tightens the leisure-seal paste-box lid so the oil will not dry.
Shen Chuan alone paces the stele-corridor outer court, silently recalling Nine-Completion Palace stroke energy.
After rain, Shen Chuan opens the study window and listens to eave water drip into the stone trough.
Shen Chuan trims a worn brush tip even, saving it for students to practice na strokes.
Another dusk, Shen Chuan sits by the Duan inkstone to rest, hearing alley-mouth cries far off.
At night Shen Chuan rises and adds a lump of charcoal to the study brazier.
Shen Chuan breaks a newly arrived Hui ink stick to test grind and notes the shade.
Shen Chuan wipes dust from the Yang Zheng characters on the old school porch plaque.
Shen Chuan carries the bamboo book chest to a dry spot and checks the bottom for worm holes.
Against bamboo shadows outside the window, Shen Chuan copies a few draft lines of the Orchid Pavilion Preface.
Shen Chuan wrings the ink-stained rag dry and hangs it under the study's rear eaves.
On a full-moon night, Shen Chuan looks from the window at the stele corridor; stone steles glow cold white.
Shen Chuan tidies the brush rack so weasel-hair tips hang downward to dry.
On the copybook flyleaf Shen Chuan writes the new year's teaching notes.
Shen Chuan polishes the two crouching-lion paperweights and presses the xuan rolls again.
Hearing abacus clicks from the alley-mouth brush shop, Shen Chuan keeps grinding ink in the Duan inkstone.
Shen Chuan glues a cracked brush washer and returns it beside the desk.
In a study corner Shen Chuan stacks a pile of student practice sheets waiting for marks.
Shen Chuan closes the bamboo blind tight against cold night wind into the Ink-Scent study.
Another Qingming, Shen Chuan sets a bunch of wildflowers on the old school porch.
Shen Chuan rolls rubbings into tubes, ties them with hemp cord, and stores them in the wall cupboard.
Shen Chuan tries a new inkstone dropper; water beads roll into a line across the Duan inkstone pool.
Shen Chuan sits silent in the study, listening to rain on bamboo leaves, long unmoving.
Shen Chuan cuts worn indigo headscarf cloth into rags—stock saved for Aqin's replacement.
At dawn, Shen Chuan patrols the stele-corridor outer court; the bamboo book chest leans by a pillar.
Shen Chuan crouches to check whether the bamboo book chest mortise joints are loose.
Shen Chuan walks to the desk corner; those earlier three leisure seals still sit strung on the red cord.
A paulownia painting box has been left under the stele corridor; gold cloud patterns flash—not Shen Chuan's bamboo book chest.
Standing in the stele corridor, Shen Chuan notes which old steles need new rubbings.
Shen Chuan hangs wet rubbing paper on the corridor wood rack.
Shen Chuan brushes stone dust from the sleeve and glances back at the study lamp.
After Grain Rain, Shen Chuan teaches passing schoolchildren to read broken characters on steles in the stele-corridor outer court.
Shen Chuan recuts sun-dried xuan into eight-line grids.
In summer heat, Shen Chuan lays a wet cloth on the Duan inkstone to cool it so ink will not cake.
Shen Chuan checks the bamboo book chest shelves and moves damp paper to the upper tier.
On an autumn night, Shen Chuan mends the copybook's loose thread binding under the oil lamp.
Shen Chuan rotates the five weasel-hair brushes so none wears too fast.
At first snow, Shen Chuan sweeps a narrow path across the study threshold.
Shen Chuan redips the leisure seals in paste and test-prints all three texts on scrap paper.
Hearing a paperweight tap the desk lightly, Shen Chuan keeps marking practice sheets.
Shen Chuan opens the stele-corridor door so a draft can carry damp from the study.
Shen Chuan hangs a rain bamboo blind on the old school porch.
Shen Chuan stores scorched ink sticks in an iron box with a dated slip.
At night Shen Chuan dreams of stele text and, waking, notes it on a blank copybook place.
Shen Chuan rinses the brush rack with clear water; pale ink threads float.
Shen Chuan wipes scroll knobs clean and rehangs them on the study's north wall.
Shen Chuan pulls new weeds from stele-corridor stone seams.
Shen Chuan hangs the weasel-hair brushes back on the rack; the numbered red papers have faded some.
Before putting out the lamp, Shen Chuan glances once more at residual ink in the Duan inkstone.
Shen Chuan folds an indigo headscarf a schoolchild left in the study and sets it at the desk corner.
Hearing the alley-mouth brush shop's closing shutters, Shen Chuan rises and locks the study.
By the charcoal fire Shen Chuan dries gloves, ready to grind ink at dawn.
Shen Chuan moves the bronze paperweights aside to show a just-written square piece.
Shen Chuan washes the palm rubbing brush and hangs it on a stele-corridor pillar.
On the last copybook page Shen Chuan draws an ink-shade comparison scale.
Silently recalling tomorrow's Eight Principles of Yong, Shen Chuan steps out of the old school porch.
Shen Chuan pushes the bamboo book chest to the wall foot, clearing floor space for practice.
Hearing a distant night drum, Shen Chuan blows out the study oil lamp.
Another rainy night, Shen Chuan alone keeps watch by the Duan inkstone, listening to eave drips until dawn.
Late at night the kitchen next to the study suddenly catches fire; thick smoke pours into the Ink-Scent study.
Firelight reddens the window paper; the Duan inkstone heats in the blast.
A crisp crack—a fine fissure splits the Duan inkstone; ink seeps into the crack.

segments.action: Outside the stele corridor comes paper merchant Lao Gu, build like Shen Chuan's, bamboo basket on the back.
The county-school prefect also arrives in gray robe and blue cap, talking beside Shen Chuan.
The prefect points at the left paulownia painting box, asking whether it belongs to the private school.
The prefect leaves; Shen Chuan alone remains in the stele-corridor outer court.
Paper merchant Lao Gu unloads a bundle of xuan, bows, and departs.
To the alley-mouth brush shop comes girl Xiaotao in a light-brown headscarf; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Aqin.
Xiaotao practices arranging the brush rack; Shen Chuan shakes his head—she is not Aqin after all.
Xiaotao shyly bows her head and returns a weasel-hair brush to its place.
Years later at dusk, Shen Chuan with gauze on the temple leans on a bamboo cane under the old school porch.
